newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan central bank won't follow Fed's rate hike.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan central bank won't follow Fed's rate hike.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank said on Wednesday it had no plans to raise the island's interest rates despite the U.S. Federal Reserve's quarter-point overnight interest rate increase.
"The Fed's interest rate hikes will not have a major impact on Taiwan," said Lee Sheng-yen, a central bank director.
"The two countries' conditions are different," Lee told reporters after the close of Taiwan's markets.

In a widely anticipated move, the U.S. central bank raised the key federal funds rate by a quarter percentage point to 5.50 percent -- the first increase since February 1, 1995 -- in an effort to stay a step ahead of inflation. The federal funds rate is the rate that banks charge each other for overnight loans.
Lee said the bank would stick to its longstanding "stable-to-loose, but not too loose" monetary policy.
The Taiwan dollar ended weaker against the U.S. dollar on Wednesday in the wake of the Fed's movement.
